subject: chopperMotorbike
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: custom chopper motorbike.
Style: Overwatch.
reasoning:
I'm planning a single, efficient module for a static vehicle model, keeping it simple without joints since props can be plain objects, using parts like lathe, sweep, extrude, and rod for the shape.

Thinking through the chopper design: a long front fork, fat rear tire, small front wheel, peanut tank, ape-hanger bars, V-twin engine, exhaust pipes, and sissy bar, styled in bold Overwatch-inspired colors with glowing neon accents. I'm working out dimensions and positions for the wheels, then building a reusable wheel helper function that lathes a tire profile and hub with spokes made from rods connecting the hub to the rim.

Still writing wheel texture and frame geometry...

Now I'm shaping the gas tank using a lathe or loft approach, building it from cross-section stations along the z-axis with varying widths and heights to get that teardrop profile.

I'm also figuring out the paint scheme with Overwatch-inspired orange and charcoal, adding a white center stripe down the tank, and planning a simple stylized logo decal with a ring shape for the tank sides.

Then I'm working on a seat piece, extruding a slab-like outline in the side profile around a given z/y range to give it proper thickness and position.

Still shaping seat outline...

For the rear fender, I'm thinking of sweeping an arc over the rear tire to form the fender geometry.

Now I'm sizing the fender geometry with boxed cross-sections and orange paint, then sketching a small front fender too. Moving to the engine, I'm placing a V-twin crankcase box near the rear axle and angling two cylinder rods upward toward front and back to form the V shape.

Adding fin rings and cylinder heads with chrome/steel coloring, then routing two exhaust pipes from the cylinders back with a glowing blue tip.

Now I'm figuring out the forks: a springer-style design with a steep rake angle, positioning the headstock and front axle to compute the steering direction.

Adding thicker lower fork sleeves, a triple tree box, and a headstock tube cylinder along the fork direction, then sketching ape-hanger handlebars with risers rising from the headstock to high grips positioned outward at the top.

Still shaping the headlight assembly...

Still placing chopper frame geometry...

Adding orange brake caliper boxes, then working on tank details like a gas cap cylinder and a small speedometer gauge placed on the tank top near the handlebar riser, calculating its position based on the tank's tapering height.

I'm placing the gauge housing as an embedded cylinder, then moving on to Overwatch-style decals: bold orange hex panels, racing stripes, a glowing blue engine core, and striped tire rims. I'm also increasing the tire lathe segments to 20 so the wheels look rounder instead of hexagonal, and making sure the lathe axis is set correctly.

Now I'm designing the texture set: a spoke decal with an orange outer ring, dark hub, and white-orange spokes, plus a logo decal with a dark circle, orange stroke, and inner white ring.

For the OW logo specifically, I'm sketching a ring with notch ticks and a wedge accent, then thinking through how decals attach to the tank surface via position/direction/size parameters, confirming the sweep surface supports decals and transparent-pixel cutting like other textures. I'm also setting up shared paint constants for the orange palette to reuse across parts.

Now I'm working out the tank's paint function, using position and normal checks to place white accents and darker lower shading, then blending warm-to-cool tones based on height with a mix/smoothstep gradient. I'm sorting out imports, pulling mix, smoothstep, paint, and noise from the main builder module, and noting that metal needs to come from the clockwork kit instead.

I'm also sketching helper functions: a tube/rod builder with default circular cross-sections, a generic part placer that can orient cylinders along different axes, and a wheel builder that lathes a tire profile outline around the axis to create the rim and tread shape.

Now I'm figuring out the hub disc placement relative to the tire sidewalls, positioning it just outside the tire's flat inner face so the spokes read correctly without clipping into the tire geometry.

Adding more wheel geometry...

Working out the headstock neck frame and handlebar geometry now, placing risers, crossbar, and grips as rods with chrome and dark coloring along defined point paths.

For the headlight, I'm calculating its lathe-axis placement relative to the fork tubes, nudging the center forward so it clears the fork geometry without overlapping the tube radius.

I'm checking the tank loft stations against the headstock and seat for overlaps, adjusting the tank's front and rear z-bounds so it doesn't collide with either part while keeping its height profile consistent.

Now I'm shifting the seat outline coordinates slightly rearward and recalculating its closed polygon points, making sure the seat sits properly on the frame's top tube near the seatpost junction without clipping through it.

I'm placing the engine block centered beneath the tank, building the crankcase as a steel-colored box, then adding front and rear cylinders angled toward the tank's underside with fin segments stacked along each cylinder and an orange head cap on top.

Now I'm adding the air cleaner and primary cover as cylindrical discs on the side of the engine, with the cover getting a logo texture applied via a circular plane oriented along its axis.

For the exhaust, I'm mirroring the design so both sides get a cover, then plotting a curved path for each side's exhaust pipe using a sequence of points running from the front cylinder exit down and back along the frame toward the rear, adjusting x-offsets to clear the rear tire.

Now I'm finishing that pipe shape with a steel-colored sweep and dark tip, adding a small glowing blue ring near the end to suggest an exhaust accent.

For the heat shield, I'm adding a second orange sweep encasing part of the pipe between two points along the path for a banded look. Then for the rear, I'm planning the axle cylinder, sissy bar, taillight, and a fender arc swept around the rear wheel center with a radius just larger than the wheel itself.

I'm now checking that the fender's top arc doesn't collide with the seat geometry, comparing their positions along y and z to see how close the seat's rear edge comes to the fender surface.

I'm working out the fender arc angles so it spans a reasonable section of the rear wheel without colliding with the seat, settling on roughly -30° to -120° using a rotation about the x-axis. There's a small gap between the seat's rear edge and the fender start, which I'll leave as-is for a bobber-style look rather than adding a connecting piece.

Checking geometry further, I find the seat bottom actually overlaps the tire's top curve near the rear, so I need to raise the seat or shift it forward slightly to clear the tire profile.

Closing the seat outline loop and checking it clears the tire geometry properly. Now tracing the seat rails back to the rear axle, confirming the rail height stays clear of both the seat bottom and the tire width at that z-position.

Sissy bar rods run from the rear axle diagonally up to a crossbar, staying outside the tire's x-range throughout, with the pad and a glowing taillight sphere mounted near the top of the crossbar.

Skipping rear shocks since it's a hardtail, and keeping the rear brake simple with a steel disc on the left side. For footpegs I'm positioning rods coming off the frame near the exhaust, but need to raise them slightly to avoid clipping the exhaust pipe which runs through that same region at a similar height.

I'm also adding an underglow strip of small blue rods beneath the engine, clear of the crankcase and pipes, plus placing a circular gauge housing near the front end with an angled face for the display.

Then I'm working out the tank-top details: positioning the gauge so it embeds into the tank surface, adding a steel gas cap sunk partway into the top, and painting a white center stripe where the surface normal points mostly upward along with a darker charcoal band along the lower sides.

Now I'm defining a two-tone paint function for the tank itself, giving it a white racing stripe, a dark charcoal trim band near the bottom, and an orange gradient fade across the rest of the surface. Next I'm starting on the front fender, positioning it over the front wheel and beginning to sweep an arc from roughly -20° to 80° to shape its curve.

Checking the fender's placement against the fork tubes, the clearances work out fine -- the fender's width and arc positions stay just clear of the fork tube radius at every height I check, so there's no geometric overlap to worry about.

Now I'm thinking through the front brake caliper and disc placement, orienting the disc texture to face outward correctly depending on which side it's mounted. For the color palette, I'm setting up dark, orange, blue, and a mottled leather tone for the different parts, and deciding the seat just needs a simple orange stripe accent rather than piping or studs. I'm also planning a glowing core effect for the engine to suggest heat.

Setting the logo circle radius, then moving into coding helper functions for rods and lathes, and starting to define a wheel-building function that constructs the tire outline and rim geometry.

Still working on tire details...

Then I'll handle engine metal materials (iron, steel, chrome), build the overall part composition, set up the loft for the tank body, and sweep a fender shape using an arc path with a box-section profile in orange paint.

I'm computing the rear and front fender arc positions with a small helper that converts center, radius, and angle into 3D points, then I'll add the sissy bar top pad as a leather-colored box before assembling everything.
